body: Alperen Şengün carried Houston on Friday night. The Rockets center scored 43 points with 12 rebounds and five assists as Houston beat the Utah Jazz 125-118 on Nov. 13 in NBA Cup group play.

He made 17 of his 24 shots, and it was only the second 40-point game of his career. Houston led 63-53 at halftime, and Şengün kept the Jazz from ever taking control after they cut the gap to three late in the third quarter.
## Why fans are buying in

The efficiency put him in rare franchise company. Şengün became the third player in Rockets history with at least 40 points, 10 rebounds and five assists on 70 percent shooting, joining Hakeem Olajuwon and Yao Ming. He did it with one turnover in 37 minutes and five offensive rebounds.

The bigger picture matters too. Houston has won three straight and moved to 10-3, third in the Western Conference. Kevin Durant added 22 points and closed the game at the free throw line, but the offense ran through Şengün in the post all night. He also helped Houston win the rebounding battle 47-41 and outscore Utah 52-46 in the paint.

In our analysis, Şengün has grown from a skilled young big man into a two-time All-Star who anchors a winning team. A night that echoes Olajuwon and Yao gives Rockets fans a natural reason to wear his name. This is our view, not a sales figure.

body: Stephon Castle set the tone early and never let up. The Spurs guard scored a season-high 32 points with six assists and five rebounds as San Antonio beat the Golden State Warriors 123-85 on Nov. 13.

He made 12 of 18 shots, went 5 of 8 from 3-point range and scored 13 of the Spurs' first 26 points. His previous high this season was 24, set against Oklahoma City on opening night, so this was a clear step up.
## Why fans are buying in

The win was San Antonio's 11th in a row, and the Spurs are now 11-2. They opened with an 18-0 run, their largest opening run of the play-by-play era, led from start to finish and built a lead as large as 43 points.

Castle is a big reason the streak feels sustainable. Last season he averaged 16.7 points and 7.4 assists, and he has grown into a primary ball handler next to Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox. On a night when Wembanyama played only 20 minutes, Castle was the one who took over, and he even finished an alley-oop lob from Wembanyama along the way.

In our analysis, Castle fits the profile of a jersey that keeps gaining fans: a young guard who just turned 22, a former Rookie of the Year and a key piece of one of the league's hottest teams. This is our view, not a sales figure.

body: Matt Boldy did it again. The Wild forward scored three goals as Minnesota beat the Toronto Maple Leafs 5-2 on Nov. 12, including the go-ahead goal early in the third period.

It was his second hat trick this season and the sixth of his NHL career. He scored once in each period, with the middle goal coming on the power play to tie the game 2-2 before he put Minnesota ahead for good.
## Why fans are buying in

The milestones are piling up. Boldy now ranks third in Wild history in hat tricks, behind Marian Gaborik and Kirill Kaprizov. He needed only 21 games to record two in one season, the quickest any Wild player has done it, one game faster than Gaborik in 2002-03.

The team around him is rolling too. Minnesota is 14-3-4, has earned points in 10 straight games and has won seven in a row on the road. Kaprizov assisted on Boldy's first goal and Quinn Hughes set up the second, giving the Wild a core fans can build a season around. Kaprizov and Hughes each extended their own point streaks to 10 games in the win.

In our analysis, Boldy has moved from a promising first-round pick to a proven scorer after a 42-goal season in 2025-26, and nights like this one make his name a natural pick next to Kaprizov's. This is our view, not a sales figure.
